verdicts.title: Exponential Lower Bounds on the Generalized Erdős-Ginzburg-Ziv Constant
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: For a finite abelian group $G$, the generalized Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv constant $\mathsf s_{k}(G)$ is the smallest $m$ such that a sequence of $m$ elements in $G$ always contains a $k$-element subsequence which sums to zero. If $n = \exp(G)$ is the exponent of $G$, the previously best known bounds for $\mathsf s_{kn}(C_n^r)$ were linear in $n$ and $r$ when $k\ge 2$. Via a probabilistic argument, we produce the exponential lower bound \[ \mathsf s_{2n}(C_n^r) > \frac{n}{2}[1.25 - O(n^{-3/2})]^r
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns exponential lower bounds for the Erdős-Ginzburg-Ziv constant on finite abelian groups $C_n^r$, with no mention of Coxeter groups, automorphism groups, or AC^0 circuit complexity. It shares only the generic notion of 'exponential lower bound' with the conjecture.

verdicts.title: Observations on Symmetric Circuits
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We study symmetric arithmetic circuits and improve on lower bounds given by Dawar and Wilsenach (ArXiv 2020). Their result showed an exponential lower bound of the permanent computed by symmetric circuits. We extend this result to show a simpler proof of the permanent lower bound and show that a large class of polynomials have exponential lower bounds in this model.
